proof:
The last base coordinate of $Q$ can be integer only at $0,1$. The sections there are exactly $Q_0$ and $[0,4]^2$, because a convex combination at an endpoint height uses only that layer. The pentagon predecessor enumerates the nine lower-layer points. The upper layer contains all $25$ points of $\{0,1,2,3,4\}^2$. The lower rows with $y=0$ and $y=-1$ each contain both first-coordinate parities, and the upper layer contains all four planar parities. Thus all eight parities occur before the extra binary product, and all $2^n$ occur after it. The hull is full-dimensional and every sampled fiber is $F$, yielding the stated $M$ and raw threshold.

For an anchor at height zero, reflected partners must both have height zero, since their last coordinates are nonnegative and sum to zero. In an extra binary coordinate their sum must equal twice the anchor coordinate, forcing them both to equal that coordinate. Thus the three retained sources are exactly the pentagon predecessor's three sources in a fixed affine block. Restricting a containing ambient halfspace to that block gives a containing closed halfspace or the whole block, and every proper block halfspace extends to the ambient space. Thus the exact optimized depths are unchanged. The outer depths exceed $(17/4)\Gamma_d v$ and the middle depth is below it, even after optimizing $x\in F$.

At the upper anchor $(2,2,1)$ the upper square lattice layer is centrally symmetric, and all of its $25$ bases in the fixed block form reflected pairs and the own base. For nonvertical caps through the point with height $g$, 6a7d56e450b3126f pays at least $2\Gamma_d v$ for each pair and $\Gamma_d v$ for the own fiber by the zero shift. Pure base caps include at least $13$ fibers in the block, with $13v\ge25\Gamma_d v$ since $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$. The same lower bound holds for all containing caps by parallel translation. The full source only adds nonnegative mass, so its depth at that point exceeds the target.
statement: Let $Q_0=\operatorname{conv}\{(-3,0),(-1,-1),(0,-1),(3,1),(2,1)\}$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}((Q_0\times\{0\})\cup([0,4]^2\times\{1\}))$, and let $F\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $v>0$ with centroid $g$, $d\ge1$. For every $n\ge3$ consider the complete product body $[0,1]^{n-3}\times Q\times F$ of mixed volume $M=2^{n-3}34v$. All $2^n$ base parities occur. At each anchor retain its own fiber and every complete reflected pair with original volumes, and optimize raw closed ambient halfspace depth over that anchor's continuous coordinate. At the original sharp raw target $2^{-n}\Gamma_d M=(17/4)\Gamma_d v$, with $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, the retained-source superlevels fail same-parity midpoint closure. In any fixed added binary block the lower-layer anchors $(-1,0,0)$ and $(1,0,0)$ have best retained depth $5\Gamma_d v$ and their midpoint has best depth $3\Gamma_d v$. The full original source has raw depth at least $25\Gamma_d v$ at the upper-layer point with base $(2,2,1)$ and continuous coordinate $g$, in any fixed added binary block.
title: Reflected-depth midpoint failure at the sharp target in all integer ranks at least three
